summary: Scheduled retention sweep removed tracehook anchors causing alerts to fire without trace links for NimbleScribe
description: Issue summary: After the scheduled retention sweep during the nightly maintenance window (2026-03-10 00:30 UTC), multiple NimbleScribe Dashboards and scheduled alerts fired with missing trace links. Alert notifications were delivered to user Slack/webhook payloads but tracehook URLs were empty or pointed to pruned anchors. Impact: Customer reports inability to jump from an alert to the related trace for debugging; several SLA-bounded alerts escalated. The console shows 0 linked traces on heatmap panels for their org for the 00:00–01:00 UTC window despite traces existing in raw ingest. Environment: prod (us-west primary org, some cross-region traffic to eu-central), dedicated account with pinned retention settings and extended rollback protection disabled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure org scoped retention policy is set to custom pruning (NimbleScribe dedicated config).
2) Wait for nightly 'retention-sweep' job to run (scheduled 00:30 UTC).
3) After sweep completes, open customer dashboard->heatmap for 00:00–01:00 UTC window.
4) Open Alerts -> Recent -> view alert payload; inspect tracehook.url field in webhook/Slack message.
5) Compare against raw trace store (S3/KV) for trace IDs referenced by alerts.
6) Observe trace links missing or 404 when accessed via console trace link resolver.

2026-03-10T00:31:05Z console-link-resolver ERROR lookup-anchor org=org-9423 anchor=tracehook:abc123 result=not-found
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 - Maya Chen: Customer reported multiple scheduled alerts with empty trace links and missing trace anchors. Provided initial screenshots of dashboard heatmap with '0 linked traces' in the affected time window.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged and escalated to infra/retention. Asked for retention-sweep logs and org configuration. Requested customer patience while we investigate.

2026-03-10 10:37 - Infra (Priya Singh): Found retention run for org-9423 deleted anchors beyond configured threshold; retention job reported anchors-evicted=3192. Investigating deletion filter logic for anchor TTL calculation.

2026-03-10 13:48 - SRE (Diego Morales): Observed retention-sweep used default tenant prefix instead of org-scoped prefix due to a recent config refactor (PR 2139). Kicking off reindex of anchor table for the affected time window as mitigation.

2026-03-11 07:22 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Sent customer a temporary workaround: re-run the alert evaluation with fallback to cached trace meta (console-side) and pointing to raw trace ids in webhook payload until reindex completes.

2026-03-12 11:15 - Customer (NimbleScribe Support Lead): Confirmed initial reindex partially restored ~72% of missing trace links for the affected window. Still seeing some orphaned alerts for eu-central traces.
investigation: Hypothesis: retention-sweep used an incorrect prefix when enumerating anchors (config key override introduced in retention-service PR 2139), causing deletion of anchors that should have been exempt for dedicated accounts.

Checked retention-service run logs and S3 delete manifests for 2026-03-10 00:30 UTC; manifests contain keys with org-9423 anchor prefix but also keys with generic prefix 'anchor/active/' which led to over-deletion.
Audit of recent deploys: retention-service 1.8.3 rolled out to prod on 2026-03-09 23:50 UTC (linked PR 2139). The deploy introduced a config layering bug when org-level overrides existed.
Cross-validated with console trace-resolver metrics: increase in 'lookup-anchor: not-found' spikes aligned exactly with retention-sweep timestamp.

Partial data recovery achieved by reindex job that reconstructed anchor entries from raw ingest metadata; reindex restored ~72% anchors for us-west, ~48% for eu-central due to delayed cross-region replication.
Root cause: config-layering bug + retention sweep lacking a dry-run/guardrail to check active alert references before prune.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 12:30 UTC): rolled back retention-service config to pre-1.8.3 values for org overrides to stop further over-deletions.

Mitigation applied (2026-03-10 14:00 UTC): kicked off reindex job for anchors for org-9423 covering 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10 window; progress monitored and validated against console-link-resolver metrics.
Workaround for customer: alert evals can be re-run against raw traces; support provided a short script to patch webhook payloads with trace_id -> raw S3 link until links are restored.

Permanent fixes planned: (1) add pre-prune guardrail to retention sweep to skip anchors referenced by active alerts (PR queued), (2) add retention-sweep dry-run mode and alerting for high-anchor-deletion deltas, (3) add post-prune verification job to ensure console link-resolver shows >=99% expected anchors.

Next actions: create PR to patch config layering (assigned to infra team), schedule across-region reindex for eu-central residuals, run customer verification call, and follow up with postmortem on Confluence.
customer_impact_summary: NimbleScribe experienced broken alert -> trace links for a narrow nightly window after a retention sweep; led to escalations and loss of debugging context. Most links restored via reindex; eu-central residuals remain and are being reindexed.
follow_up_tasks: Create and merge config-layering hotfix for retention-service (PR draft by Priya Singh).
Implement retention-sweep dry-run feature and pre-prune active-reference guardrail (eng ticket to be created).
Schedule cross-region reindex to restore eu-central anchors and validate with customer dashboards.
Draft postmortem and communicate RCA + timeline to NimbleScribe and internal stakeholders (owner: Liam O'Connor).
